newsitem.title: EU: EC REPORT WEEKLY DIARY FOR MONDAY, APRIL 7 - SUNDAY, APRIL 13.
newsitem.headline: EC REPORT WEEKLY DIARY FOR MONDAY, APRIL 7 - SUNDAY, APRIL 13.

text.p: HIGHLIGHTS
NOORDWIJK, Netherlands - EU foreign ministers conclave continues (Monday); discussions focus on the status of the inter-governmental conference on EU treaty reforms.

LEIDEN, Netherlands - EU-Rio Group meeting involving South American countries and Mexico, Panama, Trinidad, Tobago and Costa Rica (Monday-Tuesday); discussions focus on political developments in the western hemisphere and Europe; political, economic, social and environmental aspects of sustainable development; international fight against drugs and associated crime. European Commissioner Marin holds news conference on the outcome of the meeting in Noordwijk (Tuesday).

MAASTRICHT, Netherlands - EU culture ministers hold informal meeting (Monday-Tuesday); discussions focus on transfrontier fixed book prices, public broadcasting in Europe and proposed cultural paragraph in the EC Treaty. Closing news conference on Tuesday.
BRUSSELS - Inter-governmental conference representatives meet (Tuesday).

STRASBOURG - European Parliament holds plenary session (Monday-Friday). Debates focus on genetically modified maize and experiments on animals in the cosmetics field (Monday); respect for human rights, creation of a European monitoring unit on racism and xenophobia, harmonisation of the rules on driving licences (Tuesday); "auto oil" programme on car pollution, Middle East peace process, Council and Commission statements on Albania and Hang Kong (Wednesday); equal opportunity for persons with disabilities (Friday).
BRUSSELS - European Commission holds news conference on the outcome of the G-24 meeting on Bulgaria (Wednesday).
STRASBOURG - European Commission holds regular weekly meeting (Wednesday); agenda includes decisions on Fifth Framework Programme on research and technological development.
LUXEMBOURG - EU consumer ministers meet (Thursday).
MONDAY, APRIL 7

NOORDWIJK, Netherlands (EXPANDED ITEM) - EU foreign ministers hold conclave on the inter-governmental conference on EU treaty reforms (second of two days) at 0900/0700 GMT. European Commissioner Oreja attends.

LEIDEN, Netherlands - EU-Rio Group meeting involving South American countries and Mexico, Panama, Trinidad, Tobago and Costa Rica (and Tuesday). Honduras, Guyana and chairmen of the Organisation of American States, InterAmerican Development Bank, Latin American Parliament, Institute for European-Latin American Relations, European Investment Bank also attend. Discussions focus on political developments in the western hemisphere and Europe; political, economic, social and environmental aspects of sustainable development; international fight against drugs and associated crime. European Commissioner Marin holds bilateral talks with Mercosur countries (Argentina, Brazil, Uruguay and Paraguay). EU Troika holds talks with Mexican and Chilean foreign affairs ministers. Venue: Huis ter Duin.
MAASTRICHT, Netherlands - Informal Culture Council (and Tuesday). Discussions focus on transfrontier fixed book prices, public broadcasting in Europe and proposed cultural paragraph in the EC Treaty.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commissioner van den Broek meets Norwegian Fisheries Minister Karl Eirik Schuett-Pedersen. Discussions focus on the Commission's ongoing anti-subsidy and anti-dumping proceedings concerning imports of Norwegian farmed Atlantic salmon (1700/1500 GMT) - followed by a news conference at 1745/1545 GMT. Venue: Mission of Norway to the EU, 17 rue Archimede. Contact: Mission of Norway to the EU (322) 234 1111.

TOULOUSE, France (NEW ITEM) - European Commission President Santer visits Airbus Industries; addresses Toulouse Social Science University on "Building Europe together"; meets Toulouse Mayor Dominique Baudis.

BONN - European Commission hosts G7 global marketplace for SMEs conference (to Wednesday). Topics include electronic commerce policy; electronic commerce business issues; impact of electronic commerce on individual companies. Internal Market Commissioner Mario Monti attends. Contact: Sandra Helms, Empirica GmbH (49) 228 985 3888.
STRASBOURG (EXPANDED ITEM) - European Parliament holds plenary session (to Friday).
Agenda includes:
- (1700/1500 GMT) Announcement of the list of subjects for the debate on topical and urgent subjects of major importance.
- Roth-Behrendt report on the development, validation and legal acceptence of alternatives to animal testing.
- Breyer, Lannoye, des Places, Pasty, Gonzalez, Alvarez oral questions on genetically modified maize.
- Ojala recommendation on health and on the protection of workers from risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work.
STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - Following EP committees meet:
- (1900/1700 GMT) Foreign Affairs;
Economic;
External Economic Relations;
Culture;
Budgetary Control;
Fisheries.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Euro Citizens Action Service (ECAS) holds news conference on "Auto oil vote in the EP" (1100/0900 GMT). Venue: International Press Centre (IPC). Contact: ECAS (322) 548 0490.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - News conference on the annual European Assembly of Development NGOS and on the conference "Beyond Lome IV: for improved partnership in future EU/ACP cooperation" (1030/0830 GMT). Venue: International Press Centre (IPC). Contact: Valerie Van Belle, Liaison Committee of Non-Governmental Development Organisations to the EU (322) 743 8787.
SALZBURG - ACI Europe holds conference on airport development and environment issues (to Wednesday). Contact: Yevgeny Pogorelov (322) 552 0982.
BERLIN - International European Training Centre holds seminar on "Building Europe: EU enlargement and deepening". Contact: International European Training Centre (33) 4 92 15 2121.
TUESDAY, APRIL 8

LEIDEN, Netherlands (EXPANDED ITEM) - EU-Rio Group meeting involving South American countries and Mexico, Panama, Trinidad, Tobago and Costa Rica (second of two days). European Commission and the five Andes Community countries (Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru and Venezuela) hold bilateral talks. European Commissioner Marin holds news conference on the outcome of the meeting in Noordwijk (1745/1545 GMT).
MAASTRICHT, Netherlands (NEW ITEM) - Informal Culture Council (third of three days). Closing news conference on the outcome of the meeting at 1230/1030 GMT.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Inter-governmental conference (IGC) representatives meet. European Commissioner Oreja attends.

STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - Commission President Santer, Commissioners Bonino and Fischler meet to discuss possible changes to rules on production of gelatine and other beef byproducts aimed at protecting consumers from mad cow disease.
STRASBOURG (EXPANDED ITEM) - European Parliament holds plenary session (second of five days).
Agenda includes:
- (0900/0700 GMT) Announcement of the list of subjects for the debate on topical and urgent subjects of major importance.
- Vote on any request for the urgent procedure.

- (0915/0715 GMT) Roth report on human rights in the EU: the right to live and die in dignity - no to euthanasia; the right to freedom from torture and the rights of people in detection; freedom of movement; abortion in Ireland; legal rights; immigrant rights; combatting racism; social security and poverty; right to privacy; right to non-discrimination; children's rights - no to Scandinavian porn; right to a healthy environment.

- Randzio-Plath report on Commission report on jobs, the road to EMU and the 1997 annual economic report - growth, employment and convergence on the road to EMU and on the mutually beneficial effects of greater coordination of structural policies (Europe as an economic entity).
- Metten report on Commission communication on medium-term financial assistance for member states balances of payments.
- Garcia-Margallo y Marfil report on Commission communication on competitiveness and improving Europe's industry or benchmarking.
- Farassino report on a common driving licence.
- Lehne report on settelement finality and collateral security.
- Crowley report on Commission communication on simplifying the single market - SLIM: a pilot project.
- Oddy report on investment services and capital adequacy - committee power clash.
- Palacio Vallelersundi report on artists' rights and royalties - a concern for salesrooms.
- Barton recommendation for masses and dimensions of certain categories of motor vehicles and their trailers.
- (1730/1530 GMT) Question time to the Commission.
- (1900/1700 GMT) Political group meetings.
STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - Following EP committees meet:
- (1500/1300 GMT) Institutional Affairs;
Economic - Commissioner Oreja attends;
- (1700/1500 GMT) Social Affairs;
External Economic Relations - WTO Director General Renato Ruggiero attends;
- (1730/1530 GMT) Energy;
Regional;
Subcommitee on Monetary Affairs;
- (1800/1600 GMT) Petitions;
Foreign Affairs - European Commissioner van den Broek attends;
- (2030/1830 GMT) Budget.

STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - News conference prior to the offical inauguration of the European ombudsman office (1730/1530 GMT). EP President Jose Maria Gil-Robles, French European Affairs Minister Michel Barnier attend. Venue: EP, press centre.
WEDNESDAY, APRIL 9
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commission holds news conference on the outcome of the G-24 meeting on Bulgaria (1300/1100 GMT).
STRASBOURG (EXPANDED ITEM) - European Commission holds regular weekly meeting (0900/0700 GMT).
Agenda includes:
- Commissioner Cresson proposal for decision on the fifth framework programme for research and technological development.
- Commissioner de Deus Pinheiro communication on 1995 transfers in favour of traditional Caribbean banana suppliers.
- Commissioner Kinnock communication on 1997-2001 programme to promote road safety in the EU.
- Commissioners Wulf-Mathies and Flynn proposal on single document under objective 2 for Italy, Belgium, the Netherlands, Britain and France; joint support framework for Spain.
- (Possibly) Proposal to make changes to rules on gelatine and other beef byproducts aimed at protecting consumers from mad cow disease.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commissioner Brittan meets Norwegian Fisheries Minister Karl Eirik Schuett-Pedersen. Discussions focus on the Commission's ongoing anti-subsidy and anti-dumping proceedings on imports of Norwegian farmed Atlantic salmon (0930/0730 GMT) - followed by a news conference at 1015/0815 GMT. Venue: Mission of Norway to the EU, 17 rue Archimede. Contact: Mission of Norway to the EU (322) 234 1111.
THE HAGUE (NEW ITEM) - European Commissioner Brittan meets New Zealand Foreign Minister Don McKinnon at the EU-New Zealand ministerial meeting.
STRASBOURG (EXPANDED ITEM) - European Parliament holds plenary session (third of five days).
Agenda includes:
- (0900/0700 GMT) Votes on any objections concerning the debate on topical and urgent subjects of major importance.
- Joint debate on:
- Wynn report on the 1994 discharge;
- Wynn report on the 1995 discharge - general budget - Section III;
- Dankert report on the 1995 discharge - general budget - other sections;
- Blak report on the 1995 discharge - ECSC;
- Boesch report on the 1995 discharge - EDF;
- Kellett-Bowman report on the 1995 discharge - satellite body.
- Alavanos report on Euro-Mediterranean Interim Assocation Agreement between the EC and PLO;
- Council statements on the peace process in the Middle East;
- Council and Commission joint statement on Albania;
- Council and Commission joint statement on Hong Kong - followed by a debate.
- Mamere report on petrol and diesel fuels;
- Lange report on air pollution by emissions from motor vehicles;
- Eisma report on atmospheric emissions from road transport;
- Gonzalez report on CO2 emissions from passenger cars and improved fuel economy.
- Ghilardotti report on the burden of proof in cases of discrimination based on sex.
- Joint debate:
- Terron I Cusi report on free movement, Schengen and computer checks (European Information System Convention).
- Schulz report on the use of information technology for customs purposes.
- (1200/1000 GMT) Votes on reports under the cooperation, codecision and assent procedures; motions for resolutions on which the debate is closed.
- (1730/1530 GMT) Question time to the Council.
- (1900/1700 GMT) Political group meetings.
STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - Following EP committee meets:
- (1600/1400 GMT) Environment.
THE HAGUE - Dutch EU presidency hosts ministerial conference on social integration (to Friday). Reuter EC Report Weekly Diary (page 3/3 - Thursday-Sunday)
THURSDAY, APRIL 10
LUXEMBOURG - Consumers Council.
Provisional agenda includes:
- Voluntary agreements as important instruments for consumer policy - Council resolution.
- Proposal for an EP and Council directive on injunctions for the protection of consumer interests.

- Proposal for an EP and Council directive amending directive 87/102/EEC (as amended by Directive 90/88/EEC) for the approximation of the laws, regulations and administrative provisions of the Member States concerning consumer credit.
- (possibly) Report of the Commission on the application of directive 87/012/EEC concerning consumer credit.
- Proposal for an EP and Council directive on the sale of consumer goods and associated guarantees.
ROMANIA (NEW ITEM) - European Commission President Santer on official visit.
STRASBOURG (EXPANDED ITEM) - European Parliament holds plenary session (fourth of five days).
Agenda includes:
- (1000/0800 GMT) Mosiek-Urbahn report on establishing credit systems.
- Adam report on fisheries conservation.
- Baldarelli report on specific measures to encourage Italian fishermen to diversify out of certain fishing activities.
- Kindermann report on arrangements for the management of fishing effort in the Baltic Sea.
- Fontaine report on mutual recognition of higher education diplomas.
- (1200/1000 GMT) Votes on reports under the cooperation. codecision and assent procedures; motions for resolutions on which the debate has closed.

- (1500/1300 GMT) Items in the news: topical and urgent subjects of major importance such as the European Treaty, Russia, Belarus, Zaire, human rights in Cambodia, urgent humanitarian aid to Carelie (Russia) and Bulgaria.

BRUSSELS - European farm organisations COPA and COGECA hold joint news conference to introduce COPA newly elected President Luc Guyau (1730/1530 GMT). Venue: Intercontinental Europa Hotel. Contact: COPA-COGECA (322) 287 2711.

BRUSSELS - British Chamber of Commerce in Belgium holds annual banquet (1900/1700 GMT). European Commissioner Kinnock attends. Venue: Hilton Hotel. Contact: British Chamber of Commerce (322) 540 9030.
STRASBOURG - Centre of the European Bureau for Lesser Used Languages holds news conference at 1100/0900 GMT. Venue: Palais de l'Europe. Contact: Ivana Suhadolc (322) 218 2590.
FRIDAY, APRIL 11
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commissioner de Deus Pinheiro gives address at the NGO General Assembly (1430/1230 GMT). Venue: Borschette Centre.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commissioner Gradin attends European Commission hearings on "European cooperation with NGOs in the fight against traffic and sexual abuse of children".
SLOVENIA (NEW ITEM) - European Commission President Santer on official visit.
STRASBOURG (EXPANDED ITEM) - European Parliament holds plenary session (last of five days).
Agenda includes:
- (from 0900/0700 GMT) Votes on procedures without report; reports without debate.
- Schmidbauer report on disability and equality - a role for the EU.
- Needle report on EC support for regional economic integration among developing countries.
- Fraga, Estevez, Colino, Salamanca, Fantuzzy, Filippi, Happart, Ebner, Jove Peres, Lambraki, Campos, Arias Canete, Redondo Jiminez, Rosada Fernandes, Vallve joint question on rice crisis.
VENICE, Italy - First scientific congress to review measures taken by the EU to restore consumer confidence in beef after the mad cow crisis (and Saturday).

LONDON - The Royal Institute of International Affairs holds conference on "Trade and environment: conflict or compatibility?". Sessions include: trade and environment after Singapore; trade versus environment - the evidence; industry concerns; resolving trade and environment disputes; the future. Speakers include: European Commissioner Brittan. Venue: Chatham House, 10 St James Square. Contact: Sharon Moore (44) 171 957 5700.
SATURDAY, APRIL 12

PALERMO, Italy - European Cofederation of Worker's Cooperatives, Social Cooperatives and Participative Enterprises (CECOP) holds conference on "Mediterranean network of European cities and regions of the social economy" (0900/0700 GMT) (To April 15). Venue: Castello Utveggio. Contact: CECOP (322) 537 5740.
SUNDAY, APRIL 13
No events scheduled.
